description:
## Approved design (2026-09-27, proposal ../fz-xxd.5-6.html)
1. Rejection stays a fact. FunctionContract::apply already returns AppliedFunctionContract { result, satisfied, .. }; satisfied == false is "rejected", distinct from Underconstrained. apply_function_contract (jobs/semantic.rs ~1668) carries the whole application to activation_contract_return, not only .result. No new type.
2. function_contract_is_enforced (jobs/semantic.rs ~1704) checks an extern at every call site, including calls from lib code. An extern's row is exactly one call's arguments, never joined evidence. A rejected row is a fatal spec/violation naming the extern, the row and its declared domain, so it never reaches the settled-None -> none collapse (jobs/artifact.rs:78-80), the native trap for a function that never returns, or compiler2_unreachable_control.
3. The divergence machinery (none, return_diverges, unreachable_control) stays; it serves functions that really never return.
The earlier attempt (worktree fz-xxd.6, uncommitted) has semantic.rs and docs hunks that apply cleanly to the current tree. Its test moves from the deleted port_frontend_test.rs to contract_test.rs. Its fixture takes the next free number in fixtures/, not fixtures2/00559 (that number is taken).
Done when: a failing-first fixture (a user call whose row is outside an extern's contract) reports spec/violation on run, interp and build; every existing fixture stays green; each new red (e.g. a lib wrapper whose @spec is wider than its extern) is classified in a red ledger and reported, not suppressed. Whether the interpreter and native doors agree on the spawn fixtures is measured when fz-xxd.3 is built on top. One commit.

## Original report
When an extern row can never be answered, the error is silent at compile time
and a trap at runtime.

Once an extern's return is its contract applied to its row, a row outside
every clause (a truly out-of-domain call) keeps return evidence "not yet
known"; at the fixpoint that coincides with `none` (jobs/semantic.rs:208-212
comment), the continuation is specialized to `compiler2_unreachable_control`
(jobs/artifact.rs ~1484-1493), and JIT/AOT trap with SIGILL while the
compile reports nothing. Errors must be loud: a settled activation whose
return is absent because its contract rejected the row is a diagnosable fact,
not an unreachable branch.

Also observed (three-path parity, unmeasured): concurrency_ping_pong,
shared_heap_send_large_bitstring and spawn_with_captures pass on interp while
failing on run/build in the same state; the reader's hypothesis is tail
position of the call in the spawned function. The interp must fail the same
way or the others must not.

Settle with a reader, then the owner: what the compile reports (library vs
user callsite gating applies: library callsites are validated but not
diagnosed because joined activation evidence can pair uncorrelated callers),
and how "rejected" is distinguished from "not yet known" in the data model
rather than by the absence of an answer.
title: An extern row outside its contract is a silent runtime trap, not a compile error
